title: DEC-55: resolve quest in CI by exact npm install, falling back to a build of opum-ai/quest-cli at a pinned ref
description:
Implements the operator's DEC-55 ruling, relayed by opum-agent (cross-session, 2026-09-29T18:00Z; opum-doc relay ODOC-OP-2026-09-29-21, 18:00:08Z). Label, verbatim: 'Build quest from source (Recommended)'. Option text the operator saw, verbatim: 'When the declared quest version isn't on npm yet, lore's docs gate and compile smoke build quest from quest-cli's matching ref. Both version locks stay strict and Article 3 is untouched.' The same message listed the landing order: lore lands and promotes 0.12.0, then quest stages, then lore stages, e2e qualifies, and both promote.

THE DEADLOCK IT ANSWERS (measured earlier today, recorded on LCLI-653): lore at 0.12.0 cannot pass its own required contexts while quest 0.12.0 is unpublished — the LCLI-650 runtime pair lock refuses quest 0.11.0 (exit 6), so 'lore check (docs gate)' and 'compile smoke (ubuntu)' are red on the bump PR, and 'lint · typecheck · test (windows-latest)' is red for the same reason. quest cannot stage first either: its version-parity gate refuses while lore-cli MAIN reads 0.11.0 (quest-cli reproduced exit 1). Both sides' gates waited on the other's artifact.

REFS, verified by quest-cli at both and consistent with my own reads: ec79b543f4575374e4ece5f73e123fbacdab6f64 (quest-cli dev tip) and b6e1da5168a3d9b1d57eb0d3d0e6f7f6c0afebf2 (the 0.12.0 bump commit, an ancestor of the tip). At both: package.json .version = 0.12.0, src/application/version.ts QUEST_VERSION = 0.12.0, src/contract/tracker/index.ts QUEST_ADAPTER_PINNED_VERSION = 0.12.0. Source run prints the version: bun src/cli/main.ts --version -> 0.12.0. quest has runtime dependencies (commander, zod, js-yaml, @clack/prompts, string-width, unicode-case-folding), so a source checkout needs bun install first, with the repo's own pin (bun@1.4.2).

WINDOWS, still an open A/B for opum-agent: the diagnostic scratch branch diag/LCLI-653-windows-quest is measuring what provisions a quest on the windows-latest lint·typecheck·test runner (a fresh runner has none). If that job needs a DIFFERENT mechanism than the three install steps, it goes back to opum-agent as an A/B rather than being decided here.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An ADR in this repository docs bundle records DEC-55, quoting the operator label and option text verbatim, with the landing order and the pinned ref

The three quest-consuming required jobs resolve quest exactly as today when the declared version is on npm, and build opum-ai/quest-cli at the pinned ref when it is not, with the action asserting the built quest --version equals the declared version before any gate runs

Proof both ways: with quest 0.12.0 unpublished the six required contexts are green on the bump branch; and with lore package.json moved to 0.12.1 against the same source ref, lore check (docs gate) fails at exit 6 naming the pair lock rather than any build error
An independent review of the ci.yml change before it lands
Landed on dev with all six required contexts green on the head SHA; nothing promoted to main

implementationNotes:
IMPLEMENTED, not yet proven in CI. .github/actions/setup-quest (new composite action) runs today's exact `npm install -g "@opum-ai/quest@<declared>"` first, and only when that fails builds opum-ai/quest-cli at QUEST_SOURCE_REF. Wired into all three quest-consuming jobs (tracker, docs-gate, build) so they cannot drift; ci.yml carries QUEST_SOURCE_REF at workflow level; test/ci-workflow.test.ts now asserts the calls, that no job installs quest inline, that the action keeps the npm path AND the fallback's version assertion, and that the ref is a full commit SHA. ADR-0023 records the ruling, quoting the operator's label ("Build quest from source (Recommended)") and the option text verbatim, plus the landing order.

THE PIN IS ec79b543f4575374e4ece5f73e123fbacdab6f64, NOT b6e1da51. The b6e1da51 SHA relayed by quest-cli as "the 0.12.0 bump commit" does not exist on the remote at all, measured three ways: gh api returns 422 "No commit found for SHA", `git fetch origin <sha>` is refused ("upload-pack: not our ref"), and the codeload tarball is 404. That is what a squash-merged pull request head looks like after the branch is deleted — a fact worth carrying, because the same relay would have put an unreachable SHA into a workflow. ec79b543 is quest-cli's dev tip and carries 0.12.0 in package.json, src/application/version.ts and src/contract/tracker/index.ts; the action now names this failure mode in its own error, and checks `cat-file -e <ref>^{commit}` before checking out.

MECHANISM MEASURED END TO END, locally, from a clean clone rather than assumed: blob-filtered no-checkout clone 916 KB / 0.65 s (the pinned commit is already present, so no SHA-want fetch is needed — `git fetch <sha>` is refused by this remote); `sparse-checkout set src package.json bun.lock tsconfig.json` + checkout = 2.7 MB / 0.5 s (the same commit's codeload tarball is 207 MB, so the filter is doing real work); `bun install --frozen-lockfile` 23 packages / 58 ms at the pinned Bun 1.4.2; `bun run src/cli/main.ts --version` prints 0.12.0. With a shim of that run on PATH, `bun run lore check` exits 0 — 83 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings — where the same command exited 6 an hour earlier against quest 0.11.0. `lore agents --check` also exits 0. Proof in CI (both directions) and the independent review are still to run.

CORRECTION to the note above, which is itself the kind of thing it warns about. That note explained the unresolvable SHA as a squash-merge artifact ("a squash-merged pull request head ... the head you verified locally is unreachable"). Both halves of that are false, and quest-cli measured them first: the real commit is b6e1da510251fe8b75eb6fa1097158c2bfe8e5bb — the value I was given had its first eight characters right and the remaining thirty-two invented, which is a composed id rather than anything GitHub did. And GitHub RETAINS a merged pull request's head ref, so even a deleted head branch's tip still resolves. Verified here myself rather than taken on relay: gh api for b6e1da510251… returns 200 (chore(QCLI-421): bump quest to 0.12.0 for the lore/quest pair release (#443)), and b2bdfacc71113d2db06435d13aeabc41fcdab7f1 — the closed head branch's tip — returns 200 from both the commits API and codeload. So the only genuinely unresolvable thing in that exchange was a mistyped string, and the general lesson is narrower than the one I wrote: a 40-character value that resolves nowhere is usually composed rather than copied, and every query will agree about it. The three places in the repository that carried the squash-merge explanation (the action's error text, ci.yml's QUEST_SOURCE_REF comment, ADR-0023) have been corrected; ec79b543 remains the pin and the guard that checks cat-file -e before checkout stands.
